items.quote: So typically, we would like to -- we would work with -- EBITDA margin is around 28% to 30%.

items.statement: Annual capex of INR7-8 crores for adding 20-25 machines per year funded by internal accruals with 23 machines added in current year
items.quote: And we expect this 20 to 25 machine investment, which is typically around INR7 crores to INR8 crores to happen every year. This is all funded by internal accruals.

items.statement: 120 machines currently placed across India under long-term contracts averaging 5-5.5 years with reagent purchase commitments
items.quote: as of today, we have close to 120 machines all over the c ountry, which are present at various private and government hospitals and institutions, which are owned by the company, by us. And we are placing these machines on a contracted basis to these customers against a commitment of a certain amount of consumable s that they will have to buy from us every quarter and every year

items.statement: Contract durations typically 4-7 years averaging 5-5.5 years to ensure payback on machine investments
items.quote: these are typically around 5 years. Some of them are 4 y ears, some of them could be 7 years, but typically average is around 5 years - 5.5 years

items.statement: Competes with multinational companies like Abbott, Siemens, Roche but differentiated by brand-agnostic multi-vendor approach covering 25 represented companies
items.quote: So naturally, there are multinational companies like an Abbott or a Siemens or Roche, for example, these are all companies, European and American companies, which operate in this space. But wha t I feel we are slightly different because we are brand agnostic. We work with multiple brands

items.statement: Revenue grew threefold from INR35 crores to INR103 crores over last 4 years with new divisions in urinalysis, blood banking, immunology as growth drivers
items.quote: This company is -- has been in business for a long time, but it's only in the last 3 years, wherein 3 years back, our top line was around INR35 crores, which we have increased threefold to INR103 crores in the last 4 years.

items.statement: Contracted reagent rental model contributes ~50% of revenue with annuity-like characteristics, remainder from project-based business and service contracts
items.quote: Almost 50% of our top line comes from this contracted business. So this part of the business, I would say, is more like an annuity type of a business model which we are creating in which we are growing.

items.statement: Geographic strength in East and West India with North as big market and South entered 3 years ago showing significant growth potential
items.quote: It is diversified across India, but primarily our st rength lies a lot in East and I would say, East and West. North is also a big market. South is a market which we entered about 3 years back. So that has a lot of growth

items.statement: Focus on Tier 2 and Tier 3 cities for government tender opportunities and lab automation projects where large multinationals don't focus
items.quote: Our strength lies a lot into Tier 2 and Tier 3 cities. So we have done a lot of automation work there. We've done a lot of development work there. We've done projects whereby we have got a piece of land from the government, and we've actually created an entire automated path lab for them.

items.statement: Post-merger Kopran Limited will become comprehensive healthcare company with API, formulations and diagnostics under one umbrella with no other businesses outside
items.quote: Kopran Limited, becomes now the comprehensive health care company, where we are in the API business, we are in the formulations business. And now we are in the diagnostic business. So we have all the 3 segments under one umbrella. There's no other API business or pharmaceutical formulation business or diagnostics, which is out of the purview of Kopran.

items.statement: Expect to participate in 14-15% diagnostic industry growth plus new divisions and South region expansion with Kopran global support attracting more multinational partnerships
items.quote: The diagnostic industry, which is just a part of what Kopran Lab does is anyways growing at 14% to 15%. So we expect to participate in that growth. Barring that, like I mentioned, we've added a few new divisions as well into this sector, which – revenues which were not present in the last year or this year, which revenues will start to come and add to the growth story as well.

items.statement: Cold chain warehousing facilities already in place for reagent storage and supply chain management
items.quote: We have our warehousing in cold chain facilities. Cold chain has to be maintained throughout. So all that is already in place.

items.statement: Targeting 50% of PAT as dividend payout over medium term; currently slightly below that level.
items.quote: we have maintained that we want to be broadly, I mean, distributing 50% of the PAT that we generate over the medium term. Right now, we are slightly south of it, but I think in the next couple of years, we should hopefully hit that level.

items.statement: Aim to reach gross debt zero in relatively short term after achieving net debt positive.
items.quote: Step 1 is to get gross debt zero, which will hopefully happen in the relatively short term.

items.statement: Plan to maintain sales bookings at current pace of ~20,000 crores per year over next five years.
items.quote: any back-of-the-envelope calculation means you kind of try to continue at the present pace of, say, 20,000 odd crores, a good year slightly better and a bad year slightly less.

items.statement: Aspiring to achieve 45% gross margin in development business over long term.
items.quote: Overall, we are aspiring to have a 45% gross margin in the long term from our development business going forward.

items.statement: Achieved over 19,000 crores of sales bookings in current financial year.
items.quote: In sales booking, I think we have had a good year. We have almost hit 19,000 crores, over 19,000 crores of sales in this financial year.

items.statement: Launch pipeline of 37 million sq ft yielding ~114,000 crores revenue; 35% by value already launched, 15% to launch next fiscal year.
items.quote: We had presented that we will have almost 37 million square feet of projects which will be launched in the medium term, effective yielding around 114,000 crores of revenue over a period of time as and when sold. 35% of this value 114,000 crores, 35% of value worth projects have already been launched till date. Another 15% worth value will get launched in the coming fiscal year.

items.statement: Unsold inventory from launched projects worth ~25,000 crores; total gross margin potential from launched and future pipeline ~67,000 crores.
items.quote: So, overall potential of margin to be created from the projects already launched and will be launched, which are clearly defined in our thought process is almost around 67,000 crores.

items.statement: Margin growth outpacing sales growth; realized margin accrued ~25,700 crores from sales bookings, ~20,000 crores unrecognized in P&L as of Dec end.
items.quote: as on April 20, we had almost 10,000 crores of realized margin which was supposed to be recorded in our financial books of account. As I say, there is a lag in accounting. The same number we generated, we accreted around 25,700 o dd crores of margin from sales booking which has been done. We consumed in our financial statement almost 13,000 odd crores. We, as on end of December, we had over 20,000

items.statement: Premium and commercial projects targeting ~30% margin (+/-2-3%).
items.quote: the premium and commercial projects also we are saying could be in the benchmark of around 30% (+/ -2%) (+/-3%) here and there, 30% kind of realization or margin

items.statement: Capex defined as land and approval costs; investing in contiguous parcels and value-accretive land like IREO land in Sector 61.
items.quote: CAPEX, here the CAPEX, the way we have defined is land and approval cost. We continue to spend money on approvals and land wherever is required. The land acquisition will be whether to kind of improve contiguity or parcels which can have a ccretive value to the projects which we are launching

items.statement: Reassessed development potential from 169 msf to ~196 msf due to revised zoning, TOD, DR regulations; 23 msf under development, 29 msf in pipeline, 144 msf remaining for ~20 years.
items.quote: We have reassessed our potential. basis the revised zoning regulations, policies, taking into consideration TODT, DR regulations, etc., etc., and also assessing what we want to do where we feel that this 169 today on a reassessed basis could be as high as 196 million square feet.

items.statement: Generated operating cash post capex and approvals; net debt positive ~4,500 crores as of Dec end with 9,000 crores cash (7,100 crores in RERA accounts).
items.quote: Despite spending money on the CAPEX and approval cost, where the realization is going to happen in the future, we continue to generate operating cash post all expenses, post all CAPEX and approvals. We continue to generate cash for the Group. Hence, as a result, one of the stated goals which we had that we want to reduce our debt, which I covered earlier as well, we became net debt positive last y

items.statement: Net debt reduced from ~24,000 crores to ~14,000 crores over five years (~9,500 crores reduction); net debt/EBITDA down ~2.6x as of Dec end.
items.quote: We have had our focus of reducing our net debt position. Fr om almost 24,000 odd crores, we are at 14,000 odd crores net debt position in the last five years, almost reduction of 9,500 crores. And with a strong operating performance measured in EBITDA in this particular case, our net debt to EBITDA has actually come down approximately ~2.6 levels as of December end

items.statement: Targeting gross debt zero soon; currently net debt positive and building cash cushion for opportunistic acquisitions and financial income.
items.quote: We want to reach a gross debt zero benchmark, and which will happen soon. And we will be judicious and cautious on capital allocation, whether i t's shareholder return or growth

items.statement: Consistently paid dividend for 17 years; grown payout over last three years; targeting 50% PAT payout over medium term.
items.quote: We have been consistently paying dividend for almost 17 years and for the last three years at basis the performance we have actually taken care of shareholder returns in the same way and grown our dividend pay out to the shareholders as well.

items.statement: Customer mix: genuine users, investors, and speculators; actively facilitate existing customer resales (25% trade out) to avoid speculative buildup.
items.quote: So, almost about 25% of the people kind of trade out and kind of get a better option. As we have spoken around Privana and Arbour's time also in the morning, we were subscribed and oversubscribed by about almost 4x in each of these businesses, launches.

items.statement: Prioritize sales to existing customers over new bookings; monitor receivables closely to manage speculative risk.
items.quote: We very aggressively, very aggressively first say, before we go and sell, let our customers sell if that is their need or their desire, and very honestly, we go out to facilitate their sale. We do not distinguish, if at all, Aakash prioritizes the sale on behalf of an existing customer, even at the cost of a residual stock leftover in the hand of the Company.

items.statement: Execution capacity constrained by limited quality contractors; limits ability to pursue mid-income/affordable projects despite land availability.
items.quote: our constraint is our ability to successfully execute. The ecosystem around us of execution, unfortunately, is not keeping pace with the needs of our industry, maybe other industries. And therefore, what we need to be careful about is that while all these dreams are predicated on my ability to turn it around w ith lower margins, somebody behind me has to back me up to accept my sort of proposition

items.statement: Focus on premium/luxury segments (5-7 cr+ tickets); mid-income project Garden City Enclave delivered at 1.4-1.5 cr (now 2.4-2.5 cr) but not actively pursuing more due to execution constraints.
items.quote: We have done a project recently, it's almost getting delivered now, which is called Garden City Enclave, Devinder has done it. It's a bunch of low -rise houses, 4 floors very, very sort of carefully and consciously planned within a price point which we sold, correct me if, it was INR 1 crores something was the price point? So, INR 1.4 crores to INR 1.5 crores we sold it at, not too far back, about

items.statement: Pre-sales (sales bookings) KPI: ~19,000 crores in FY25; launches Privana South, Privana West, Dahlias oversubscribed 4x.
items.quote: Our launches, as you are already aware, have been well received, whether it is Privana South, Privana West, you got some statistics from A akash, was significantly oversubscribed. We did, if I may use the word, rationalize, we had to kind of prioritize whom we want to give, and that's always a good position to be in.

items.statement: Second-market price appreciation: Arbour up ~8,000/sq ft, Privana up ~4,000/sq ft in ~2 years.
items.quote: As we are today, as we stand today in about 2 years, Arbour has an upside of almost about INR 8,000 a square foot, which is trading in second markets, and Privana is upwards of INR 4,000.

items.statement: Advocate deep focus on core NCR markets over geographic diversification; cite Oberoi Realty and Lodha as examples of community-focused success.
items.quote: So, anybody who has, maybe Lodha is doing it with Palavas, takes a sizable chunk, remains deeply invested, starts thinking 20, 30, 40 years, lives through it, takes the good times, the bad times, stands with the customer, that is where the real reputation comes, that's where the real financial upside comes.

items.statement: Execution risk from limited contractor ecosystem constrains volume growth and mid-income foray; speculative buyer risk monitored via receivables.
items.quote: If the construction industry here kind of opens up, that the delivery problems start going away from your mind, possibly companies like us can look at doing this. But right now, you have to keep your fingers crossed. It's a risky player.

items.statement: Cash flow projection: ~43,000 crores from launched projects; net cash generation ~25,000 crores post opex/capex/tax; total potential ~50,000 crores including new pipeline.
items.quote: So, with in this period, we are looking at anywhere almost 50,000 crores of cash balance in a way because we started with 9,000 crores in the medium term.

items.statement: Geographic focus remains NCR (Gurugram, Delhi, Noida), Chandigarh, and early-stage Mumbai; no immediate plans for new development geographies.
items.quote: NCR will be a good market for us. North India, more around Chandigarh, we will continue to be there. Mumbai, we are dipping our toes in the water. Let's hope the results are encouraging. So, I think these will be principally the markets we will remain focused on.

items.statement: Targeting INR 10,000 crore rental revenue by FY30 with portfolio doubling to 70 million sq ft
items.quote: Overall, if I were to look at this 5 year and all our projects kind of come out on time, we are looking at almost INR 10,000 crores of rental revenue by FY30 plus minus 6 months, 1 year, whatever.

items.statement: Planning INR 20,000 crore capex over next 5 years for identified rental and hospitality projects
items.quote: We are looking at almost investing INR 20,000 crores, INR 12,000 crores in the DCCDL portfolio and INR 8,000 crores across rental and hospitality business in the DLF portfolio as well, so INR 20,000 odd crores ballpark number over the next 5 years for identified projects.

items.statement: Office portfolio to grow from 39 million to 60 million sq ft; retail to triple from 4 million to 12 million sq ft over 5 years
items.quote: We are looking at adding another 21 million square feet for projects which are already under pipeline or planned for. This portfolio itself will become 60 million square feet and we will see a fairly sharper growth in the retail portfolio as well from another 4 million, we look at almost tripling this number to almost 12 million over the next 5 years or so.

items.statement: Occupancy at 93% weighted average across office and retail; office ex-SEZ at 97%, retail at 98%
items.quote: One thing which I missed talking about is our occupancy level. We are at almost 93% on a weighted average basis across retail and office. Our office portfolio is at short 93% and if I were to exclude the SEZ portfolio, it would be almost close to 97%. Retail is healthy at 98%.

items.statement: New projects 95% pre-leased, providing visibility on near-term rental income
items.quote: All our new projects are almost 95% pre-leased. So I think we are a reasonable place for all the new projects which are going to come for occupation.

items.statement: Net debt to EBITDA at 3.6x as of December end; targeting steady state of 3x
items.quote: However, our financial performance has been reasonably good, very very steady across the years and our net debt to EBITDA ratio is approximately 3.6 as on December end which to my mind is well benchmarked and we are fairly comfortable with this number.

items.statement: Targeting net debt to EBITDA of 3x as steady state for rental business
items.quote: Another aspect is the net debt to EBITDA. We continue to look at almost the net ratio of 3 of net debt to EBITDA as a steady state and that is what we kind of aspire to be at this point of time.

items.statement: Residential demand accelerating, not pent-up; younger buyers (28-30 years) entering market
items.quote: I think demand is accelerating and not kind of catch this thing.

items.statement: Residential price growth at 10-12% annually; rapid increases beyond this uncomfortable
items.quote: So, if the price points remain somewhere as a growth rate of, say, 10%, 12% generally, I think the industry is safe and we are comfortable and our margins will continue growing. Rapid price increases beyond this point would be a little uncomfortable, somewhat unnecessary.

items.statement: Sales pace to flatten; launches front-ended with 50% soon, balance in nearer future
items.quote: What we have told you right now is be prepared for a flattening of the sales curve. If it gets front-ended, good for everybody. Launches will tend to get a little bit front-ended, 50% being done soon, and hopefully, the balance in the nearer future and not at the end of this period.

items.statement: Company geared for 4-5 residential launches and 2-3 commercial project starts per year
items.quote: I think you will see that happening anywhere next year in my opinion, because some approvals have kind of seem to have got bunched off and delayed. I hope they come through soon. So, I think that the number of 2-3 low level, I think 4 or 5 big and small will take place in the development bu siness itself and 2 to 3 starts in the so -called commercial business

items.statement: 85 million sq ft premium land bank identified; 5-10% may be disposed, 20-30% upskilled to luxury/ultra-luxury
items.quote: So I am not really worried about a 30% plus number. I don't think it represents anything which is something which the company should not be aggressively pursuing, but I know it is going to go up overtime because of all the efforts we will put in here.

items.statement: Focus on software services and customer living experience over hardware differentiation
items.quote: Really what we have brought as DLF to the table, which I think has been well appreciated by my customers, by hopefully the industry, I do also believe even global players have taken notice, is not too much of a change on the hardware, but an intense focus on the software, whether it's customer focus during the process or the post sales living experience.

items.statement: Execution and delivery critical to unlock RERA cash flows; profits recognized with lag
items.quote: All the money which goes in, goes into the RERA account. So, today the cash flow just goes into RERA account. I can throw my weight around and say it's mine, but actually it's not. So, unless you don't execute and don't deliver, you don't get the cash flow.

items.statement: Office concentration risk mitigated by diversified tenant base, financial strength, and land flexibility for residential conversion
items.quote: Worst comes to worst will be that you convert them to residential opportunities. It may happen sometime. Markets may take a turn fo r this thing. If it so happens we are okay with it. So that is why I am trying to say that all our lands below our office or retail buildings are quality lands capable of any use, so we have thought about the downsides quite a

items.statement: Delhi opportunities limited to peripheral areas; central Delhi land mostly government-owned
items.quote: for Delhi, my main point is that all the land of any significance in better locations belongs to the government. So the government has to do two things. It has to first loosen this policy and make the development business attractive and then secondly has to make sure that the land is offered to it

items.statement: Welcoming new developer entrants (former channel partners, contractors); no red flags observed
items.quote: I welcome those guys. I don't want to take names, but I am familiar with a few of them which you are talking about. I wish them well. If they can put it together, the industry always needs some new blood coming in and if they can bring it and become good quality developers more than happy.

items.statement: Yield on cost for rental capex ~25% (3-4 year payback excluding land cost)
items.quote: So we are, those benchmarks are what we start with, but hopefully we will be slightly better in terms of return to cost, but r emember in our case, we are fortunate right now to ignore land. So if you ignore land on construction, we certainly feel that money we spend, we should get back hopefully in 3 years, in some cases it becomes 4 years, yes

items.statement: No strategic shift to flex/managed offices; already provide extensive building management services
items.quote: Firstly, the good news is we are semi in the managed office businesses because we are not just making a building and walking away. Luckily for us, in all our buildings, we have sufficient amount of management presence. We manage them actively, we amortize them a lot.

items.statement: Rental revenue to double in shorter period; growth pace sustainable with strong pre-leasing
items.quote: Certainly the rentals would definitely hopefully, let us say, double in a shorter period of time and that kind of pace can be continued.

items.statement: Construction contractor shortage limits ability to pursue new land opportunities
items.quote: If the construction industry here kind of opens up, that the delivery problems start going away from your mind, possibly companies like us can look at doing this. But right now, you have to keep your fingers crossed. It's a risky player. So, we are in the immediate future going to utilize our lands, what we have. I don't think we will go looking for new opportunities in that sector.

items.statement: Targets 45% gross margin in development business and INR 25,000 crores surplus cash from launched projects
items.value: 45% gross margin; INR 25,000 crores surplus cash
items.quote: We are targeting almost 45% gross margin in the development side of business with INR 25,000 crores of surplus cash potential from existing already launched projects.

items.statement: Targets annual rentals of INR 10,000 crores by FY30 exit and group PAT and cash flow to grow 2X or more in next five years
items.value: INR 10,000 crores annual rentals; 2X+ PAT and cash flow growth
items.quote: Annual rentals of around INR 10,000 crores in the next five years exit next by FY30 and our group PAT and cash flow to grow 2X or 2X plus in the next five years or so.

items.statement: Aims for gross debt zero in DevCo soon and group gross debt close to zero in next five years
items.quote: As stated above, in development side we would like to get to a gross debt zero position soon. And overall in the next five years on a group level, our gross debt position should be close to zero.

items.statement: Plans to distribute 50% of PAT as dividend with 15-20% dividend growth over next five to six years
items.quote: We look at almost distributing 50% of our PAT as dividend return, which will translate to 15% to 20% growth over the next five, six years on the dividend payout as well.

items.statement: Annuity business CAPEX of INR 20,000 crores over next five years (INR 12,000 crores DCCDL, INR 8,000 crores DLF sites)
items.quote: CAPEX INR 20,000 crores in the annuity business, INR 6,000 to INR 7,000 crores in the development business. The CAPEX of INR 20,000 crores is going to help us build the base to kind of have accelerated growth in the rental business post FY30 as well.

items.statement: Development business CAPEX of INR 6,000-7,000 crores over next five years; total group CAPEX INR 26,000-27,000 crores
items.quote: INR 7,000 – INR 8,000 crores would be CAPEX for the development business. So CAPEX alone will be around INR 26,000 – INR 27,000 crore.

items.statement: Cost to complete launched development projects is INR 20,000 crores; total construction spend including development obligations INR 40,000-50,000 crores
items.period: as on date / next five years
items.quote: This INR 20,000 crores you are talking about? Murtuza: Yes. Badal Bagri: This is cost to complete all the projects which have been launched in the development side business as on date. All cost complete

items.statement: 73 million sq ft developed rental area by end of five years plus 60+ million sq ft available for development
items.value: 73 million sq ft developed; 60+ million sq ft pipeline
items.quote: The rental business which we talked about, annuity business, we would have 73 million s quare feet of developed area by end of five years and another 60 plus million square feet available for development

items.statement: Over 200 million sq ft combined development potential across DevCo and RentCo after executing identified projects
items.quote: We continue to hold extremely strong, valuable land bank with both DevCo and RentCo, annuity business and development business combined over 200 million square feet of development potential pending, which will remain pending after which executing all the identified projects.

items.statement: Rental business will follow clients to new geographies like Bangalore and Mumbai when opportunities arise
items.quote: But in rental business, we may follow our clients. But that time and a good opportunity will tell you.

items.statement: Expects marginal price escalation in the INR 75,000 crores medium-term development potential
items.quote: The expectations are fairly marginal I would say. Fairly marginal.

items.statement: Residential pricing in India at INR 15,000-17,000/sq ft ($200) far below global cities at $500-1,000/sq ft; bulk of India at INR 7,000-8,000/sq ft ($100)
items.quote: Today, I hope most of the people start delivering what they are promising. They're quite nice apartments and the price point is, let's say about INR 15,000 – INR 16,000 a square foot. I mean, maximum 20,000, but INR 15,000 – INR 17,000, you get something nice here. What is INR 15,000 – INR 17,000 here? $200? You'll get nothing but $200 in 90% of international cities.

items.statement: Views managed office operators as partners bringing flexibility and new tenants; monitors exposure prudently due to their fluid model and lower capitalization
items.quote: We look at the managed space providers as our partners and sort of serve a purpose of providing flexibility and new tenant introduction into our portfolios. Their business model is slightly more fluid, slightly more short-term, and the capitalizations of some of them are slightly lesser than some of these established multinationals.

items.statement: Does not measure market share; focuses on utilizing own land bank rather than chasing JV/JDA projects for pre-sales
items.quote: We don't measure market share. This is not a business of market share, number one. Number two, as I said, we did our bit a few decades ago. We don't really need to do it aggressively today.

items.statement: Post-RERA development model is tough; banks cannot fund land purchase, money stuck in RERA accounts forces developers to high-cost NBFC borrowing or equity dilution
items.quote: The model of development with post RERA is really a tough model. I will tell you very frankly, I somehow can't figure out how you can enter this business because your project cannot generate the capital required to buy that land. The banks are not authorized to provide capital to buy the land. The money gets stuck into the RERA account.

items.statement: DevCo gross cash at least INR 25,000 crores; RentCo net debt lower than that; group net cash higher than RentCo net debt
items.value: INR 25,000+ crores DevCo cash; RentCo net debt < DevCo cash
items.quote: Puneet, the gross cash that we are saying DevCo business will have would be at least INR 25,000 crores. And hopefully the RentCo net debt should be a number less than that. So on a group basis, our net cash should definitely be higher than the RentCo net debt.

items.statement: RentCo debt will increase in absolute value but not drastically; DevCo will generate cash; financial leverage not a focus due to accounting standards skewing ratios
items.quote: It will in fact increase by absolute value but not too much. DevCo will start throwing out cash. So this equation I do believe at the end of the day would change but not materially so.

items.statement: No plans to buy out GIC stake; will provide liquidity options if GIC seeks exit, possibly through listing
items.quote: I am not in sort of push to consider anything to do with GIC in buying out or this or that, no. Our understanding is very clear that if and when they wish to seek options of liquidity, we shall do our best to provide the same to them. It could be through listing.

items.statement: Hospitality classified as annuity business; few thousand crores CAPEX over next 5 years to serve ecosystem; may pursue third-party hotel opportunities opportunistically
items.quote: Frankly, in the next 5 years, a few thousand crores will be utilized just to build CAPEX for that purpose alone. That money cannot be measured simply by what it earns. It has to be measured by what earnings it provides to the ecosystem it serves.

items.statement: Conservative debt strategy provides comfort to withstand bad times without interrupting plans; keeps cash reserves for unforeseen events like COVID
items.quote: We have a huge, huge way to go before we can claim to be anything of world class in terms of infrastructure, standards, quality, pricing, availability, everything. And I think we still see a 20 – 30 year clear sort of run rate ahead of us. We can have bad timings and that's why while we are following a very conservative debt strategy, we do believe it gives us the comfort to see through any bad ti

items.statement: Land value appreciation at 10-12% annually for customers; inherent land value increase significantly higher
items.quote: 10%, 11%, 12% is the average value increase in the hands of my customers. My inherent land value increase is significantly greater.

items.statement: Mumbai project is a test; 3-5 years to decide on deep entry or limited execution; not material to overall business
items.quote: 3 to 5 years, either we will take deep steps into the market or we will kind of satisfy ourselves with executing limited projects very successfully. I don't know the answer to this. It's not material to our business, to be honest with you.

items.statement: Rental yields at $2-3/sq ft; comfortable with steady rental increases covering cost inflation rather than significant rerating
items.quote: I am quite comfortable if we don't have significant rental deltas but have consistent and steady increase. We watch our paybacks. Inflation has affected us. Certain changes affect us. So because of that, our costs do go up. So far, the rentals are covering that. I hope they continue to cover it.

items.statement: Development business aims to be net working capital positive; holds cash as discipline against optimism and unforeseen risks
items.quote: Our business by nature is a business where you are optimistic, you have to dream a bit, you have to believe a bit. When you start believing it too much is when you get into a lot of trouble. So I think I am just kind of putting some guide lines.

items.statement: Enhanced soft services and wellness offerings under 'Thrive' brand to improve tenant experience and retention
items.quote: We have reinvested and right now established a brand. The test samples have been successful. Now, we are going to grow it aggressively called thrive wh ere we feel we will be able to provide a very good wellness option to our customers

items.statement: Land bank quality allows conversion to residential if office/retail demand weakens; all lands below buildings are versatile quality lands
items.quote: All our lands below our office or retail buildings are quality lands capable of any use, so we have thought about the downsides quite a bit. To be conservative, but I don't think such pessimism is really necessary as of now.
